proposals.before: Ha Panlong, Guo Xing, Ren Ju, Ye Daxiong, Ma Liangzhu, Ben Jinzhong, and Liu Shun
proposals.after: Ha Panlong, his son Guo Xing, Ren Ju, Ye Daxiong, Ma Liangzhu, Ben Jinzhong, and Liu Shun
proposals.reason: Chinese 哈攀龍子國興 marks Guo Xing as Ha Panlong's son; the idiomatic English drops that kinship.

proposals.before: Chieftain Nuo'erta, with their ruler Mengbo dead, sent the envoy Deluyun to ask for a withdrawal.
proposals.after: Chieftain Nuo'erta, on the orders of their ruler Mengbo, sent the envoy Deluyun to ask for a withdrawal.
proposals.reason: Chinese 以其酋懵駁命 means by Mengbo's order/command (命), not that Mengbo was dead.

proposals.before: The chieftain Nuo'erta, because their ruler Mengbo had been killed, sent an envoy named Deluyun to the army to beg that troops be withdrawn.
proposals.after: The chieftain Nuo'erta, by order of their ruler Mengbo, sent an envoy named Deluyun to the army to beg that troops be withdrawn.
proposals.reason: 命 here is 'order/command'; the literal wrongly renders Mengbo as having been killed.

proposals.before: Guo Xing took a detour through Akemuya Ravine toward Ma'erdike stockade; finding Cebudan's forests too deep and paths too narrow for a main column, he left two thousand men with Hailancha to assault Ma'erdike.
proposals.after: Guo Xing took a detour through Akemuya Ravine toward Ma'erdike stockade; finding Cebudan's forests too deep and paths too narrow for a main column, he led two thousand men to assist Hailancha in assaulting Ma'erdike.
proposals.reason: Chinese 乃將二千人佐海蘭察 means he led two thousand men to assist Hailancha, not that he left the men with Hailancha.

proposals.before: In year twelve he was ordered to Jinchuan under Governor Zhang Guangsi.
proposals.after: In year twelve he was ordered to campaign against Jinchuan under Governor Zhang Guangsi.
proposals.reason: Chinese 命徵金川 means ordered to campaign against Jinchuan; the idiomatic omits the campaign sense retained in the literal.

proposals.before: Now, employing Ju and the others separately — none of them served in the Zhandui campaign and have no restraints — they should be encouraged to press forward boldly.
proposals.after: Now, employing Ju and the others separately — none of them served in the Zhandui campaign and they have no restraints — they should be encouraged to press forward boldly.
proposals.reason: After 'none of them served', the coordinated clause needs an explicit subject ('they have'), not bare 'and have'.

proposals.before: At that time the emperor had just ordered Ju's formal appointment; Commissioner-General and Grand Secretary Neqin reported Ju's death in service; the emperor, reading the memorial, wept and also issued an edict: "Ju, stirred by loyal indignation, welcomed death as though it were sweet; yet I, on account of petty rebels rampaging, sent a worthy minister into peril — the thought cuts deeply!
proposals.after: At that time the emperor had just ordered Ju's formal appointment; Commissioner-General and Grand Secretary Neqin reported Ju's death in service; the emperor, reading the memorial, wept and also issued an edict: "Ju, stirred by loyal indignation, welcomed death as though it were sweet; yet I, on account of petty rebels rampaging, sent a worthy minister into peril — the thought cuts deeply!"
proposals.reason: The literal opens a quotation for the edict but never closes it, unlike the Chinese closing ！」 and the idiomatic.

proposals.before: Summoned to court, he had his son Jijun appointed an imperial guardsman with the blue arrow feather and ordered to escort Daxiong to his new command.
proposals.after: Summoned to court, his son Jijun was appointed an imperial guardsman with the blue arrow feather and ordered to escort Daxiong to his new command.
proposals.reason: Chinese 官其子 marks an imperial grant of office to the son, not an act Daxiong himself effected; the idiomatic 'he had his son appointed' reverses the agency.

proposals.before: Jijun went to Changde to fetch the family; en route he borrowed money from the local people, and Daxiong reported it.
proposals.after: Jijun went to Changde to fetch the family; en route he borrowed money from Hui people, and Daxiong reported it.
proposals.reason: 假回民金 specifies Hui (回民) people as the lenders; 'local people' drops that ethnoreligious marker.

proposals.before: Jijun reached Changde to meet the family; on the way he borrowed money from the people; Daxiong reported this.
proposals.after: Jijun reached Changde to meet the family; on the way he borrowed money from Hui people; Daxiong reported this.
proposals.reason: Literal likewise omits 回民; restore Hui people for source fidelity.

proposals.before: Liangzhu asked to shift the Rongbu column to the rescue; Governor Zhang Guangsi refused, and Xing was lost to the enemy.
proposals.after: Liangzhu asked to shift the Rongbu column to the rescue; Governor-General Zhang Guangsi refused, and Xing was lost to the enemy.
proposals.reason: 總督 is Governor-General; rendering it as Governor understates the office.

proposals.before: In year thirty he followed General Ming Rui against Burma, attacked Manjie, took sixteen wooden palisades, killed three rebels, was wounded in the forehead, and fought again the next day still bandaged.
proposals.after: In the thirtieth year of Qianlong (1765) he followed General Ming Rui against Burma, attacked Manjie, took sixteen wooden palisades, killed three rebels, was wounded in the forehead, and fought again the next day still bandaged.
proposals.reason: 三十年 follows the Qianlong 13 dating earlier in the same biography and should be rendered as Qianlong 30 (1765), matching the packet's own conversion pattern.

proposals.before: Knowing Shun's knowledge of the frontier, the emperor transferred him to regional commander of Xining in Gansu.
proposals.after: Because Shun was familiar with frontier conditions, the emperor transferred him to regional commander of Xining in Gansu.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English awkwardly doubles 'knowing/knowledge'; the Chinese 上以順熟邊情 states the emperor acted because Shun knew frontier affairs.

proposals.before: Summoned to the Rehe traveling palace, he was granted audience, assigned to the Gate of Heavenly Purity, rewarded with sable and silver, and sent back to the army.
proposals.after: Summoned to the Rehe traveling palace, he was granted audience, ordered to serve at the Gate of Heavenly Purity, rewarded with sable and silver, and sent back to the army.
proposals.reason: 乾清門行走 is an assignment to serve at the Qianqing Gate; 'assigned to the Gate' omits the service duty made explicit in the literal.

decisions.reason: s0002 reads 哈攀龍子國興; 子 marks Guo Xing as Ha Panlong's son, which the idiomatic listing omits.
以其酋懵駁命 is 'by order of their ruler Mengbo' (命 = command); the idiomatic wrongly makes Mengbo dead.
The same 命 is Mengbo's order, not his death; the literal 'had been killed' invents a killing absent from the Chinese.
乃將二千人佐海蘭察 means Guo Xing led two thousand men to assist Hailancha; 'left … with Hailancha' reverses the agency of 將 and 佐.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 乃將二千人佐海蘭察攻瑪爾迪克

decisions.after: In Qianlong 12 (1747), he was ordered to campaign against Jinchuan under Governor-General Zhang Guangsi.
decisions.reason: 命徵金川 orders a campaign against Jinchuan, while 總督 is Governor-General; naming Qianlong 12 (1747) follows the biography's dating context.
After 'none of them served…', the second verb needs an explicit subject; bare 'and have' is ungrammatical English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 皆未從征瞻對，無所掣肘

decisions.reason: Chinese closes the edict with ！」; the literal opens the quotation but never closes it.

decisions.after: Daxiong entered court for an audience. His son Jijun was appointed an imperial guardsman with the blue arrow feather and ordered to escort Daxiong to his new command.
decisions.reason: 官其子 is an imperial grant to Daxiong's son; naming Daxiong explicitly avoids the proposal's dangling modifier and preserves the subject of 入覲.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 入覲，官其子繼鈞藍翎侍衛，命送大雄上官

decisions.reason: 假回民金 names Hui people (回民) as the lenders; 'local people' erases that ethnoreligious marker.
Literal likewise drops 回民; restoring 'Hui people' matches the Chinese.

decisions.after: Liangzhu asked to move the Rongbu column to the rescue; Governor-General Zhang Guangsi refused, and Zhang Xing fell into the rebels' hands.
decisions.reason: 總督 is Governor-General, and 興 refers to Zhang Xing; naming him removes an otherwise ambiguous one-word reference.
In this biography's Qianlong-era sequence, 三十年 is Qianlong 30 (1765); clarifying the reign and western year matches the chapter's conversion practice and the Chinese year.
上以順熟邊情 is a causal 以-clause (because Shun knew frontier conditions); 'Knowing Shun's knowledge' is broken English that obscures that cause.
命乾清門行走 is adequately rendered by 'assigned to the Gate of Heavenly Purity'; changing to 'ordered to serve' is a preferred calque of 行走, not a factual correction.
